sections.h2: Which desk bills and collects property tax in Crawford County?
sections.html:
Crawford County divides the work between two offices. One mails and collects the bills, and the other decides what each parcel is worth. Sellers end up calling both.

The commissioner's counter is at 640 GA Hwy 128 in Roberta, staffed weekdays from 8:15 in the morning until 4:45 in the afternoon, except holidays. The phone is (478) 836-3575. The county site says this office handles real and personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber bills, and that it does not process appeals or name and address changes.

The assessors' side, reached at (478) 836-2800, takes returns, exemption applications and written appeals. A house inside Roberta may also owe city tax, which is collected at Roberta City Hall.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Crawford County land and roads?
sections.html:
Crawford County lies in west central Georgia and is counted in the Macon metropolitan area. Knoxville holds the courthouse, and Roberta is the biggest town. With about 325 square miles of land and roughly 37 people per square mile, most parcels are rural.

The eastern fall line cuts the county roughly in half, which leaves the north hillier and the south flatter, with more cropland. Interstate 75, U.S. 80, U.S. 341 and State Routes 42, 96 and 128 cross the county, and the Fall Line Freeway touches a small part of the south along State Route 96. Houston County gave up the land for it in December 1822.

Monroe, Bibb, Peach, Taylor, Macon and Upson counties border it, and Houston County meets its far eastern edge. Lizella and Zenith are unincorporated, and Musella is a census-designated place alongside Knoxville. Many parcels carry acreage, so a seller of part of a tract should ask the assessors how a split is handled.

sections.h2: How do federal numbers describe Crawford County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates 12,206 people and 5,388 housing units for July 2025. About 81.4 percent of homes here are owner-occupied, the highest share among the four Georgia counties in the same comparison.

  • Typical home value (2020 to 2024 survey period): $164,100.
  • Typical rent over that period: $914 a month.
  • Households: 4,441, averaging 2.71 people each.
  • Residents who had not changed addresses in the prior year: 94.0 percent.
  • Mean trip to work: 33.0 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 29.

Very few households relocate, and the drive to work averages over half an hour. Rent is far under the $1,626 shown for Dawson County in that table.

sections.h2: When is Crawford County property tax due?
sections.html:
The county site gives December 20 as the usual due date for real estate. Bills normally go out in mid-October, addressed to the person who held title at the start of the year.

The Department of Revenue's county sheet adds that a county may move that date to December 1 or November 15, or split billing into installments, and that interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark. Read the date printed on your own bill before scheduling a closing.

  • Interest on late tax runs at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, accrued monthly. The rate is reset each calendar year from the first weekly Federal Reserve posting.
  • An added 5 percent penalty applies at each 120-day mark after the due date.
  • FiFa charges are added once the bill goes on the General Execution Docket.
  • Mobile homes taxed off-digest are due May 1, then draw a 10 percent penalty and 1 percent interest a month.

Lenders do not get bills from this office, according to the county. Owners with escrow should check that the servicer has the figures, and anyone whose mailed copy never showed up can request a duplicate.

sections.h2: How does Crawford County set the amount of tax?
sections.html:
The tax equals 40 percent of the assessors' fair market value times the millage rate, using the parcel's worth on January 1. County commissioners set one rate, the school board sets another, and Crawford County adds its garbage fee to the same statement.

A rollback rate is the rate that would collect last year's revenue after values rise. Going above it means three public hearings. The 2023 notice from Crawford County announced a levy 26.5 percent over rollback, with hearings on August 1, 15 and 29 at the courthouse at 100 GA Hwy 42 S in Knoxville. A 2021 notice shows the county also publishes its tax digest and five-year levy history in its news section.

Ask the tax commissioner for the millage on your parcel. An old bill is a poor guide, because both boards can change their rates every year.

sections.h2: What is the process to contest a Crawford County valuation?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Tax Assessors. The tax commissioner's office will not take it. The clock is 45 days, counted from the day the assessment notice was mailed, and the county says notices generally arrive in spring.

A return filed in the first three months of the year lets you state your own value and sets up the notice. Owners are not required to file every year. Because the state sheet says the appeal must carry a postmark inside the window, a mailing receipt is worth keeping.

If the Board of Assessors leaves the value unchanged, ask the assessors' office what the next level of appeal is and what deadline applies. A seller who gets a spring notice shortly before listing the house should read it closely, since the value feeds that year's bill and a buyer's expectations.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Crawford County owner claim?
sections.html:
Homestead is the main one. Applications are taken all year, though April 1 closes the digest. The applicant must own the house, live in it on January 1, name Georgia as legal residence, and hold title personally. Service members must also name Georgia as home state.

  • Added relief begins at 62, and the applicant must have reached that age by January 1 of the filing year.
  • Disability claims need statements of total disability from two separate sources.
  • A veterans exemption is also offered through the assessors.
  • Agricultural, preferential, conservation use, historic and tax-exempt status all run through the same office.

Under the state sheet, skipping the application counts as waiving the exemption. An heir who takes over a house should ask the assessors about filing in the new owner's name instead of assuming the old one carries over.

sections.h2: How should unpaid Crawford County tax be handled before a sale?
sections.html:
Ask the tax commissioner for a written payoff before signing anything. The office tells people mailing overdue payments to phone first, because penalties and execution charges move the total.

The statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, so a seller closing in the fall is the named taxpayer for that year. Put the split in the sale contract and ask the closing agent to carry the payoff into the settlement numbers.

Mobile homes add a step. All taxes must be paid and a current decal displayed before one is moved out of the county.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Crawford County property tax?
faqs.a: In person at 640 GA Hwy 128, Suite 134, in Roberta, or through the mail to P.O. Box 634 at the same town. The office takes checks, cash, money orders and credit or debit cards, and the county site links to online payment.

faqs.q: Does Crawford County mail my tax bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: No. The county states that it does not bill lenders. If you pay through escrow, make sure the servicer has the amount, and phone (478) 836-3575 for a duplicate if yours never arrived.

faqs.q: Who do I contact to change the owner name on a Crawford County parcel?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessors, at (478) 836-2800. Notices go to the last known address of the January 1 owner, and the commissioner's desk does not process these updates.

faqs.q: Can I still file for homestead in Crawford County after April 1?
faqs.a: You can still turn in the form, but it will not reach that year's digest, because April 1 is the cutoff.

faqs.q: Is there any way around a missed Crawford County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The state's county fact sheet says the appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing date, so a late one risks being turned away. Keep the notice, note the mailing date, and send your written appeal to the Tax Assessors well before the last day.
